names.name: Tanya Dewan
names.best: Says exactly what the site does; verb-first, imperative like Jom/Cuba; all three domains free.
names.catch: 'Dewan' alone also means any hall, and 'Dewan Rakyat' is the official chamber, so a little official-sounding; two words.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Rekod Rakyat
names.best: Neutral, civic, names the record idea; all three domains free.
names.catch: Less of a verb, so it is harder to say 'I Rekod-Rakyat-ed it'; 'Rekod' alone suggests health records (Ministry of Health app RekodSaya exists) or criminal records; 'Rakyat' appears in many government apps (Respons Rakyat, Rakyat App).
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Semak
names.best: Very short, a real everyday verb for checking.
names.catch: Slang 'semak' = cluttered/annoying; semak.com taken; MySPR Semak (election commission voter-check app) exists, so semantically close to an official service.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Rujuk
names.best: Everyday word for looking something up, ideal for students/journalists; .my and .com.my free.
names.catch: In Malay family law 'rujuk' = reconciling with a divorced spouse (religious connotation); generic; rujuk.com taken.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Petik

names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Dewanku
names.best: Warm, personal, 'the House' idea; all three domains free.
names.catch: Could read as an official parliament app (the official app is 'Parlimen Malaysia'); 'dewan' also means wedding/event hall so SEO noise; no meaning of asking.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Lantai
names.meaning: 'The floor' (as in 'on the floor of the House'; 'lantai' = floor)
names.best: Short, evocative of the debating floor; .my free.
names.catch: Mostly known as plain 'floor' (tiles/flooring businesses), so confusing; lantai.com taken; says nothing about asking.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Soalan

names.catch: Generic and confused with exam question banks (soalan SPM sites) and with Parliament's own 'soalan lisan'; soalan.com taken.

names.name: Ask Hansard
names.best: Clear in English; Hansard is the word journalists and students know.
names.catch: English-only and longer; 'Hansard' may confuse casual Malay readers; askhansard.com and askhansard.my are taken (.com.my free), so the clean .my is gone.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Tanya Hansard
names.best: Blend of Malay verb and the English term; all three domains free; stronger tie to the record than Tanya Dewan.
names.catch: Three-plus syllables heavier; 'Hansard' reads as official; the official Digital Hansard portal (hansard.parlimen.gov.my, relaunched June 2026) is similar-sounding so mistaking is possible.
names.clash_notes: Web search (standard) found no exact-name Malaysian app/site/party for it; search tool is weak, so treat as not verified, not as cleared.

names.name: Cakna

top3.name: Tanya Dewan
top3.why: It is the only name that is a verb plus the House, people can say 'cuba tanya Dewan', and .my, .com.my and .com are all free.

top3.name: Rekod Rakyat
top3.why: Neutral, civic and about the record itself, with all three domains free, though it is a noun rather than a verb.

top3.name: Dewanku
top3.why: Short, warm and easy to say with all three domains free, but it needs a tagline to carry the asking idea and could pass as an official app.

method: Run 2026-11-26. .com: Verisign RDAP (rdap.verisign.com/com/v1/domain/<name>.com), 200 = taken, 404 = free. .my and .com.my: whois over port 43 to whois.mynic.my ('is available for registration' = free; a 'Domain Name:' record = taken), because rdap.org has no .my service and rdap.mynic.my is a web page, not RDAP; tested with google.com.my (taken) and a nonsense name (free). Hyphenated variants not checked (none needed). Nothing registered or reserved, no forms. Clash research: a handful of standard web searches (the tool returned few exact matches), so absence of clashes is unverified; trademark (MyIPO) and social handles not checked. Dropped from the 16 checked: Jejak and Sumber (both taken on all three domains).
